clue.text: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite

definitions.text: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite

parts.words: States of the Continental Divide? Just the opposite
parts.note: rather than a split across the Continent, think of the states of the Continent joined together in one bloc

explanation.surface: A geography question about a great watershed, then a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental Divide' suggests the American watershed; 'just the opposite' turns a divide into its contrary, so the states of the Continent (Europe) are joined rather than split.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloc of member countries on the European mainland formed a political and economic partnership, the opposite of division.

clue.text: Newspaper creating uniform criterion

parts.note: making something uniform or level is evening it out
a standard is a criterion to measure against

explanation.surface: A newspaper setting a consistent benchmark for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A London daily paper sold in the afternoon and evening, hence its title.

clue.text: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?

definitions.text: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?

parts.words: Old soldier put on fire engine from time to time?
parts.note: a fire engine is repainted in its traditional colour now and then, so it is given a fresh coat of that colour

explanation.surface: A retired serviceman occasionally riding on a fire truck.
explanation.walkthrough: British soldiers once wore scarlet tunics; a British fire engine is painted red, so it periodically gets a new coat of red paint.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry of past centuries were known for their scarlet tunics, giving their nickname.

clue.text: An affair, naturally, that's routine

parts.note: an affair is a matter, a business or concern
of course means naturally, as expected

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging that a love affair is perfectly normal and unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' wants to mean a romance; here it is just a matter, a piece of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as a matter of normal habit or procedure is described with this idiom for the routine.

clue.text: To the extent fashionable furniture's N right

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
a sofa is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A remark about how far a trendy furniture choice is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a conjunction meaning 'to the degree that', it stands for the phrase of extent.

clue.text: G Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things S like this?

definitions.text: Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things S like this

parts.words: Perpetual harmony through total abstention from things S like this
parts.note: a peaceful relationship where no angry remark is ever spoken, and also one where nobody ever solves a puzzle like this one

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping the peace by giving up a pastime entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase describes a couple who never quarrel; 'things like this' is the crossword itself, so never doing one also keeps the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying two people never had an angry exchange describes lasting harmony, and the last word doubles as the puzzle being solved.

clue.text: Good objective set by monarch, male or female

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A good aim fixed by a king or queen, said to concern men or women.
explanation.definitionFit: The category of being masculine or feminine is the grammatical and social classification of sex.

clue.text: Sticking with advantage he has before I have

parts.note: in tennis the score after deuce, advantage, is shortened to ad
contracted to he's
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A tennis player clinging on, holding advantage before the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue and tape are sticky; the adjective describes something that clings.

clue.text: Measure of power one had in talk arranged with two

indicators.note: the words are rearranged, set out in a different order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A single person sitting in on talks set up with two others, a measure of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns I (one), TALK and TWO into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of power equal to a thousand watts.

clue.text: Provide a fine President of the US (but not now)

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

parts.words: President of the US (but not now)
parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US President in the 1970s, a former holder of the office

explanation.surface: A fine levied on a former American President.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or supply something, as in affording an opportunity.

clue.text: Girl that's cut short by military commander

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander

indicators.note: the word is docked of its final letter, cut short at the end

parts.note: that, with 's for 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: A girl's story curtailed by an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga was a commander in the Ottoman Empire; 'by' means placed next to, and the 's of "that's" is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in the crime writer Christie.

clue.text: E 13 A very old and spiteful woman, one performing minor job

parts.note: a cat is slang for a malicious woman
the Roman numeral I stands for one
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: An ancient, malicious old woman doing a small job.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or subsidiary occupation followed besides one's main work.

clue.text: Ruddy good chap, not the Oxbridge type

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour
a brick is a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A red-faced, decent fellow who did not go to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick university is one of the British civic universities founded in the 19th century, contrasted with Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic universities built of brick are the standard contrast with the ancient Oxford and Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Number ten in deadlock

definitions.meaning: in rugby union the fly-half, also called by this name, wears shirt number 10
an impasse where neither side gives way

explanation.definitionFit: A rugby position wearing the 10 shirt, and a stalemate between opponents.

clue.text: Followers of William, Greg and others

definitions.meaning: William the Conqueror led the invading army from Normandy in 1066
Greg is the Australian golfer with that surname, and others share it

explanation.definitionFit: The Conqueror's invading army in 1066, and people surnamed like the golfer Greg.

clue.text: Advance into stronghold, not recalled

indicators.note: one word is placed into the middle of the other

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
to go is to move forward or advance

explanation.surface: An army pushing into a fortress, a move nobody remembers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one did not remember has slipped the memory.

clue.text: Curl of hair enclosed in covering letter

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, held within them

explanation.surface: A lock of hair tucked inside the letter accompanying a job application.
explanation.definitionFit: A small curl or lock of hair.

clue.text: Female part in American Dream

indicators.note: a part of the words that follow is taken, a piece within them

explanation.surface: A woman playing a role in a story about the American Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name.

clue.text: Instrument is initially measuring a living creature

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument

indicators.note: taking only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A scientific instrument that first takes measurements of a living thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Any individual life form, plant or animal.

clue.text: Information about one kind of literature

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Background facts on a literary type.
explanation.definitionFit: A category of artistic work, such as tragedy or romance.

clue.text: Unconcerned member of Parliamentary opposition?

definitions.meaning: offhand, showing a careless lack of concern
in the English Civil War the Royalists who fought the Parliamentarians had this name

explanation.definitionFit: Means offhand or careless, and was the name for a Royalist fighting Parliament in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Hold as national hero

definitions.meaning: a wrestling hold applied from behind the opponent's arms and neck

explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip, and the British admiral killed at Trafalgar, a national hero.

clue.text: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think

definitions.text: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think

parts.words: Impartial but not unconcerned, despite what some may think
parts.note: the word means having no personal stake, and is often wrongly used to mean lacking interest

explanation.surface: A usage note correcting a common confusion between two words.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a usage note: the word means impartial, though many use it to mean bored or uninterested, which is properly 'uninterested'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no personal stake in a matter is neutral, which is its strict sense, distinct from bored.
